name: How much should I budget for a whole-home renovation in Los Angeles in 2026?

mainEntity.name: How much should I really budget for a whole-home renovation in Los Angeles if I want to avoid underestimating the total cost?
mainEntity.text: How much should I really budget for a whole-home renovation in Los Angeles if I want to avoid underestimating the total cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A realistic budget depends on whether you are updating finishes, reworking layout, or doing a full gut renovation. In Los Angeles, many whole-home projects fall into one of four bands: cosmetic refresh, standard full remodel, heavy renovation, or luxury rebuild-level work. The biggest cost drivers are square footage, structural changes, kitchen and bath count, plumbing and electrical replacement, finish level, and whether the home needs new systems throughout. A smart budget should also include design fees, permit costs, inspections, temporary housing, and a contingency of at least 10% to 20%. If your home is older or has hidden issues, contingency can matter even more. The safest approach is to ask for a line-item estimate that separates design, demo, structural work, MEP upgrades, finishes, and allowances so you can compare bids accurately.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most whole-home renovations in Los Angeles should be budgeted by scope, not just square footage. Cosmetic projects often start around $150,000 to $300,000, mid-range full renovations commonly run $300,000 to $500,000, and heavy or luxury remodels can reach $800,000 to $1.5 million or more.
